info.name: GearUp API
info.description:
Complete collection for the GearUp sports & outdoor gear rental platform.

**Base URL**: {{baseUrl}} — defaults to http://localhost:5000/api/v1. Update to match your actual app.ts mount prefix.

**Auth model**: JWT access + refresh tokens, set as httpOnly cookies on login (not returned in the response body for client-side reading). In Postman, enable the cookie jar (Settings → General → 'Automatically follow redirects' + cookies enabled) so logging in once carries your session across every other request in this collection automatically.

**Roles**: CUSTOMER, PROVIDER, ADMIN — set at registration. Routes marked with a required role will 403 if the logged-in user doesn't match.

**Response shape (success)**:
```
{ "success": true, "statusCode": 200, "message": "...", "data": {...}, "meta": {...} }
```
**Response shape (error)**:
```
{ "success": false, "statusCode": 404, "message": "..." }
```

**Collection variables** ({{gearId}}, {{categoryId}}, {{orderId}}, {{userId}}) — populate these after creating/listing resources so dependent requests (update, delete, get-by-id) work without manual edits.

---
### Production-readiness notes (this revision)
- Fixed: every request under **Payments** pointed at `/payments/*`; the server mounts that router at `/api/v1/payment` (singular). All four requests now hit the real path.
- Added `pm.test()` assertions and automatic variable capture (`categoryId`, `gearId`, `orderId`, `paymentId`, `userId`) on list/create responses, so you can run folders top-to-bottom via Collection Runner without manually copying ids.
- Added two environments (see the exported `.postman_environment.json` files): **Local** (`http://localhost:<PORT>/api/v1`) and **Production** (placeholder — fill in your real deployed URL). Never put real secrets in an environment file you plan to share.
- The Stripe Webhook request is included for completeness but cannot be exercised correctly from Postman directly — see its description for the `stripe listen`/`stripe trigger` workflow.
- `provider.gear` bulk-create returns `{ count }`, not the created records, so `gearId` can't be captured from that response — run **Get My Gear** right after to populate it.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Login and token refresh. Both set httpOnly cookies rather than returning tokens for client-side storage, protecting against XSS-based token theft.

request.description:
**Public.**

Validates credentials and, on success, sets two httpOnly cookies:
- `accessToken` (short-lived, e.g. 1 day)
- `refreshToken` (long-lived, e.g. 7 days)

Both are also returned in `data` for reference/debugging, but the cookies are what actually authenticate subsequent requests.

**Body params**
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| email | string | yes | Must be a registered account |
| password | string | yes | Plaintext; compared against the stored hash |

**Errors**: 404 if no user with that email exists; 400 if the password doesn't match; 403 if the account is banned.

**Note**: a 404 specifically for "no such email" vs a distinct error for "wrong password" lets a caller enumerate registered emails. If that matters for your threat model, make both cases return the same generic "Invalid email or password" message/status.

exec: // Convenience only: primary auth is via httpOnly cookies (cookie jar).
// These variables let you manually add an Authorization: Bearer header
// if you're testing against a client that doesn't send cookies.

request.description:
**Public (relies on cookie).**

Reads the `refreshToken` httpOnly cookie, verifies it, and issues a new `accessToken` cookie — lets the client stay logged in past the access token's short expiry without re-entering credentials.

No body required — the refresh token is read from the cookie automatically (requires cookie jar enabled in Postman).

**Errors**: 401 if the refreshToken cookie is missing, expired, or invalid.

item.name: Users
item.description: Account registration for customers and providers.

request.description:
**Public.**

Creates a new account. Role selection happens here — the platform has no separate 'become a provider' upgrade flow, so choose the correct role at signup time.

**Body params**
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| name | string | yes | Display name |
| email | string | yes | Must be unique |
| password | string | yes | Hashed before storage — never stored/returned in plaintext |
| phone | string | depends | Adjust to your actual userRegisterSchema rules |
| address | string | depends | Adjust to your actual userRegisterSchema rules |
| role | enum | yes | `CUSTOMER` or `PROVIDER` (not `ADMIN` — admins are seeded/promoted separately) |

**Errors**: 409/400 if the email is already registered (depends on your service's uniqueness check).

Exact (case-insensitive) brand filter, separate from free-text search
Defaults to true if omitted — unavailable gear is hidden from public browsing unless explicitly requested

request.description:
**Public.**

All query params are optional and combine with AND logic (e.g. search + categoryId + minPrice all apply together). Returns `data` as an array of gear items with `category` and `provider` (id/name/email only) included, plus `meta` for pagination.

**Validation**: minPrice cannot exceed maxPrice — returns a 400 if violated.

**Public.**

Returns full gear details with `category` and `provider` included.

**Errors**: 404 if the id doesn't exist.

item.name: Provider
item.description: Gear inventory management and order fulfillment for the PROVIDER role. All routes require an authenticated provider.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "4-Person Camping Tent",
  "description": "Waterproof, easy setup, fits 4 people comfortably.",
  "brand": "Coleman",
  "image": "https://example.com/images/tent.jpg",
  "rentalPrice": 25.5,
  "stock": 5,
  "condition": "GOOD",
  "categoryId": "{{categoryId}}"
}

request.description:
**Requires PROVIDER role.**

`providerId` is set automatically from the authenticated user — never accepted from the request body.

**Body params**
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| name | string | yes | 1–200 chars |
| description | string | yes | |
| brand | string | yes | |
| image | string (url) | no | |
| rentalPrice | number | yes | Must be > 0 |
| stock | integer | yes | Must be >= 0 |
| condition | enum | no | NEW \| GOOD \| FAIR \| DAMAGED — defaults to GOOD |
| categoryId | uuid | yes | Must reference an existing category |

**Errors**: 400 if categoryId doesn't exist.

exec: // which returns only { count }, not the created rows/ids. gearId can't be
// captured from this response — call 'Get My Gear' below to populate it.

request.description:
**Requires PROVIDER role.**

Returns every gear item owned by the authenticated provider (regardless of isAvailable), including category info. Not paginated.

**Requires PROVIDER role + ownership.**

All fields optional — send only what you want to change. Unknown fields are rejected (strict schema); this prevents overwriting protected fields like `id`, `providerId`, or `createdAt`.

**Updatable fields**: name, description, brand, image, rentalPrice, stock, condition, categoryId, isAvailable.

**Errors**: 404 if gear doesn't exist; 403 if it belongs to a different provider; 400 if categoryId is provided but invalid.

**Requires PROVIDER role + ownership.**

If the gear has any orders currently in an active state (PLACED, CONFIRMED, PAID, or PICKED_UP), it is **soft-deleted** (`isAvailable` set to false) instead of removed, so in-flight rentals stay intact. Otherwise it's hard-deleted.

**Errors**: 404 if not found; 403 if it belongs to a different provider.

**Requires PROVIDER role.**

Returns every rental order that contains at least one of this provider's gear items — including orders where other providers' items are also present, but `rentalItems` on each order is filtered down to only this provider's line items.

Each order includes `customer` (id/name/email/phone), `rentalItems` (with nested gearItem id/name/image), and `payments`. Check `returnRequested` / `returnRequestedAt` on each order to see which ones the customer has asked to return.

**Requires PROVIDER role + at least one gear item in the order.**

Allowed transitions (anything else is rejected with 400):
```
PLACED    -> CONFIRMED | CANCELLED
CONFIRMED -> CANCELLED
PAID      -> PICKED_UP
PICKED_UP -> RETURNED
```
Note: PLACED -> PAID happens automatically via the Stripe/SSLCommerz webhook, not through this route.

Setting `CANCELLED` or `RETURNED` automatically restocks the gear (`stock` incremented by the order's quantity for each item).

**Body params**
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| status | enum | yes | Must be a valid next state per the transition map above |

**Errors**: 404 order not found; 403 if none of the order's items belong to this provider; 400 if the transition isn't allowed.

item.name: Rentals (Customer)
item.description: Order placement and lifecycle actions for the CUSTOMER role.

request.description:
**Requires CUSTOMER role.**

Atomic transaction: validates stock for every item, computes `totalAmount` from each gear item's `rentalPrice × quantity × number of rental days`, decrements `stock` for each item, and creates the order with status `PLACED`. If any item fails (not found, unavailable, insufficient stock), the entire transaction rolls back — no partial orders.

**Body params**
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| startDate | ISO date | yes | |
| endDate | ISO date | yes | Must be after startDate |
| items | array | yes, min 1 | Each item: `{ gearItemId: uuid, quantity: positive integer }` |

**Errors**: 404 if a gearItemId doesn't exist or isn't available; 409 if requested quantity exceeds current stock.

**Requires CUSTOMER role.**

Returns all orders placed by the authenticated customer, newest first, including `rentalItems` (with gear id/name/image) and `payments` (id/status/amount/method/paidAt).

**Access**: the order's own customer, any provider with a gear item in the order, or an admin.

Returns full order details including all rentalItems (full gearItem objects, not a select subset), payments, and customer contact info.

**Errors**: 404 if not found; 403 if the requester is none of the allowed parties.

**Requires CUSTOMER role + ownership.**

Only allowed while order status is `PLACED` or `CONFIRMED` — once payment has gone through (`PAID` or later), cancellation via this route is blocked (would need a refund flow instead). On success, restocks every item in the order and sets status to `CANCELLED`.

No body required.

**Errors**: 404 not found; 403 not the owner; 400 if status is already PAID/PICKED_UP/RETURNED/CANCELLED.

**Requires CUSTOMER role + ownership.**

Signals to the provider that the customer intends to return the gear. This does **not** change the order's `status` itself — it only sets `returnRequested: true` and stamps `returnRequestedAt` with the current time. The provider still must call **Update Order Status** with `RETURNED` to finalize the actual transition (which is what triggers restocking and unlocks reviews).

`returnRequested` is a permanent record and is never reset back to false, even after the provider confirms the return — it preserves whether the return was customer-initiated or provider-initiated for later reference.

No body required.

**Preconditions checked**:
- Order status must currently be `PICKED_UP`
- Order must have at least one `Payment` with status `COMPLETED`
- A return must not already be requested on this order

**Errors**: 404 not found; 403 not the owner; 400 if not PICKED_UP or not paid; 409 if already requested.

**Requires CUSTOMER role.**

Only allowed once the referenced rental order's status is `RETURNED`, and only for a gear item that was actually part of that order. One review per (customer, gear item, rental order) combination — renting the same gear again in a separate order allows a separate review.

**Body params**
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| gearItemId | uuid | yes | Must have been part of the given order |
| rentalOrderId | uuid | yes | Must belong to the requesting customer and be RETURNED |
| rating | integer | yes | 1–5 |
| comment | string | yes | Max 1000 chars |

**Errors**: 404 order not found; 403 not your order; 400 if order isn't RETURNED yet, or the gear wasn't part of this order; 409 if already reviewed this exact (gear, order) pair.

item.name: Payments
item.description:
Stripe / SSLCommerz payment session creation and webhook confirmation.

**Fixed in this revision:** requests in this folder previously pointed at `/payments/*`, but `app.ts` mounts the payment router at `/api/v1/payment` (singular) — every request here was 404ing against the real server. Paths now match the Express mount.

request.description:
**Requires CUSTOMER role + ownership of the order.**

Creates a Stripe PaymentIntent (or SSLCommerz session) for the given order's `totalAmount`, attaching `rentalOrderId` as metadata so the webhook can later match the payment back to the correct order. Returns a client secret / redirect URL depending on `method`.

**Body params**
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| rentalOrderId | uuid | yes | Must belong to the requesting customer, status should be CONFIRMED |
| method | enum | yes | STRIPE \| SSLCOMMERZ |

**Errors**: 404 order not found; 403 not your order; 400 if order isn't in a payable state.

exec: console.log('Open this Stripe Checkout URL in a browser to complete payment:', json.data.url);

header.description: Generated automatically by Stripe/Stripe CLI — cannot be manually constructed for a real test. Use `stripe trigger payment_intent.succeeded` via the Stripe CLI instead of calling this from Postman directly.

request.description:
**Not directly callable from Postman** — included here for documentation completeness only.

This route must be mounted with `express.raw({ type: 'application/json' })` (before the global `express.json()` middleware) since Stripe's signature verification requires the exact raw byte payload.

On `payment_intent.succeeded`: marks the matching `Payment` as `COMPLETED`, sets `paidAt`, and flips the `RentalOrder.status` to `PAID`.
On `payment_intent.payment_failed`: marks the `Payment` as `FAILED`.

**To test locally**: run `stripe listen --forward-to {{baseUrl}}/payments/webhook` in one terminal, then `stripe trigger payment_intent.succeeded` in another.

**This request cannot be triggered manually from Postman in a way that will pass signature verification.** The route reads the raw body and verifies `stripe-signature` against `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; Postman can't produce a valid signature for arbitrary JSON. To test this flow, use the Stripe CLI: `stripe listen --forward-to localhost:<port>/api/v1/payment/webhook` and `stripe trigger checkout.session.completed`.

**Requires CUSTOMER role.**

Returns the authenticated customer's full payment history across all their rental orders.

**Access**: the payment's owning customer, or an admin.

**Errors**: 404 not found; 403 if not the owner or an admin.

item.name: Admin
item.description: Platform oversight — all routes require ADMIN role, enforced globally via `router.use(auth("ADMIN"))` on this module.

request.description:
**Requires ADMIN role.**

Returns every registered user (customers, providers, and admins).

**Requires ADMIN role.**

Admins cannot change another admin's status — attempting this returns 403 regardless of the requested status. Setting `accountStatus` also syncs `isActive` (`true` only when status is `ACTIVE`; `false` for `INACTIVE` or `BANNED`).

**Body params**
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| status | enum | yes | ACTIVE \| INACTIVE \| BANNED |

**Errors**: 404 user not found; 403 if target user is an ADMIN.

**Requires ADMIN role.**

Unlike the public gear listing, this returns every listing regardless of `isAvailable` — useful for moderation.

**Requires ADMIN role.**

Returns every rental order platform-wide, across all customers and providers, with customer, rentalItems (+ nested gearItem), and payment included.

**Requires ADMIN role.**

**Body params**
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| name | string | yes | |
| slug | string | yes | URL-friendly identifier, should be unique |
| description | string | yes | |
